title: Elizabeth I becomes queen, 1558 — from the Tower to the throne in four years
sources: Wikipedia: Elizabeth I — queen of England and Ireland from 17 November 1558 until her death in 1603, aged 25 at her accession; the last and longest-reigning Tudor; her mother Anne Boleyn was beheaded on 19 May 1536 when Elizabeth was two years and eight months old, and Elizabeth was declared illegitimate; after Wyatt's rebellion (January–February 1554) she was interrogated and on 18 March 1554 imprisoned in the Tower of London, protesting her innocence; Simon Renard argued Mary's throne would never be safe while Elizabeth lived; supporters including Lord Paget convinced Mary to spare her for lack of hard evidence; on 22 May she was moved to Woodstock for almost a year under house arrest, cheered by crowds along the way; she never married; the Spanish Armada was defeated in 1588; the Elizabethan era of Shakespeare, Marlowe and Drake
Wikipedia: Mary I — died on 17 November 1558, aged 42, at St James's Palace
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1989 students march in Prague, beginning the Velvet Revolution; 1796 French forces win the Battle of Arcole

post.facebook:
On this day in 1558, Elizabeth I became Queen of England and Ireland — four years after she had been locked in the Tower of London.

Her mother, Anne Boleyn, was beheaded before Elizabeth turned three, and she was declared illegitimate. When her half-sister Mary was queen, Wyatt's rebellion broke out in 1554; Elizabeth was questioned and sent to the Tower on 18 March, protesting her innocence. Mary's confidant Simon Renard argued that her throne would never be safe while Elizabeth lived. But there was no hard evidence, and Elizabeth's friends at court persuaded Mary to spare her. She spent almost a year under house arrest at Woodstock — and crowds cheered her along the way.

On 17 November 1558 Mary died, aged 42, and Elizabeth became queen at 25. She ruled for 44 years, never married, saw off the Spanish Armada, and gave her name to the age of Shakespeare and Drake.

Also on 17 November: students marched in Prague, starting the Velvet Revolution (1989), and Napoleon won the Battle of Arcole (1796).

17 November 1558: Elizabeth I became Queen of England at 25 — four years after she was locked in the Tower of London. Her mother Anne Boleyn had been beheaded and she was declared illegitimate. After Wyatt's rebellion in 1554 she was sent to the Tower, protesting her innocence, and her sister Mary was warned her throne would never be safe while Elizabeth lived. Spared for lack of evidence, she was cheered by crowds on her way to house arrest. She ruled for 44 years, never married, and saw off the Spanish Armada.

Also on 17 November: the Velvet Revolution begins in Prague (1989) and the Battle of Arcole (1796).
